title: The indefinite article: un, uno, una, un'
rule: A / an. Masculine: un, or uno before s + consonant, z, gn, ps, pn, x, y. Feminine: una, or un' before a vowel. No plural: the partitive (dei, delle) does that job later.

head: Definite
Indefinite
Before
Examples
rows: un letto, un tavolo, un portone
un armadio, un appartamento, un amico
masculine + s+cons., z, gn, ps, pn, x, y
uno stendino, uno zaino, uno gnocco, uno psicologo, uno yogurt
una stanza, una chiave, una zia

blocks.title: The apostrophe test
blocks.text: Un' is una with its a dropped, so only feminine nouns ever get it. [[un amico]] (m.) has no apostrophe because un has lost nothing; [[un'amica]] (f.) has one. If you see un' before a word, the word is feminine.
Uno is also the number one

items.t: C'è un bagno. / C'è un solo bagno.
items.n: There's a bathroom. / There's only one bathroom.
items.note: un = a, and also one; solo makes it "only one"
alone, the number is uno, feminine una

blocks.title: When Italian leaves the article out
blocks.text: Professions and nationalities after essere: [[Sono pasticcera.|I'm a pastry chef.]], [[È canadese.|He's a Canadian.]] English puts a / an there; Italian doesn't. Unit 4 returns to this.

items.why: No article with a profession after essere.

items.n: a flat · a water heater · a chair · a (female) friend

items.why: The apostrophe gives it away: idea is feminine (l'idea, le idee).

items.q: There's a table and a chair.
